text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- MUTUAL FUNDS' ASSETS HIT 107 BLN REAIS
Assets at mutual funds reached 107.1 billion reais at year's end, a rise of 63.38 percent over 1995, according to data by the National Association of Investment Banks (ANBID).
-- RTZ TO INVEST $300 MLN IN THE COUNTRY

British RTZ will invest $300 million in Brazil between 1997 and 1998. Lord Holme of Cheltenham, the group's foreign affairs director, confirmed in Brasilia the firm's "great interest" in the privatization of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD).
-- IF FOREX REMAINS UNCHANGED, INFLATION OF 6.0 PCT IN 1997
Sao Paulo may have this year a civilized inflation of just 5.0-6.0 percent, considering the maintenance of the current foreign exchange policy, says the Economic Research Institute (Fipe).
On Wednesday, Fipe announced 1996's inflation rate at 10.03 percent, the lowest since 1950.
-- CONDE GIVES UP SELLING BCN
After four months of negotiations, BCN president Pedro Conde gave up plans for a partnership with Banco BBA Creditanstalt.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- DEPUTIES ASK FOR FUNDS IN EXCHANGE FOR RE-ELECTION
Government deputies are asking for funds in exchange for their support to the re-election amendment. Three deputies of Mato Grosso state asked for funds for hospitals.
-- 300 GAS STATIONS TO PAY FINE DUE TO FUEL PRICE HIKE
More than 300 gas stations will pay daily fines of 10,000 reais due to excessive increases in gasoline prices.
O GLOBO
-- DIFFERENCE BETWEEN BANKING SERVICE FEES HIT 19,900 PCT
Banking service fees charged by Brazilian banks vary 19,900 percent from one bank to another. Government banks charge the lowest fees.
-- PRESIDENT BACKS RE-ELECTION FOR ALL

In a move to soothe tempers among pro-government lawmakers, President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said "the re-election is for all," and not only for the president. Inocencio Oliveira, Liberal Front Party (PFL) leader in the Chamber of Deputies, had said he expected Congress to block the re-election for state governors and mayors.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
